summary.intent: The user was managing a multi-phase development project using a GSD (Get Stuff Done) planning system, aiming to complete Phase 38 (retire deprecated web services) and plan Phase 39 (user-configurable vault parameters) concurrently via background agents.
summary.outcome: Phase 38 plan files were fully written (4 PLAN files, RESEARCH, VALIDATION), Phase 39 context was captured with key UX decisions, and both executor/planner background agents were spawned. The Phase 38 planner agent got stuck on the git commit step but its deliverables were already on disk.

repo: Project uses a structured .planning/phases/ directory with numbered phases, each containing PLAN.md files, RESEARCH.md, VALIDATION.md, and a CONTEXT.md for decisions.
Phase dependencies are tracked explicitly (e.g., Phase 39 depends on 38, Phase 38 depends on 37).
Phase 39 vault settings will auto-populate defaults from hardcoded values: 30d retention, 10 versions, 15m cooldown, soft-delete.
Server-side RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS env var is being deprecated in favor of user-configurable settings.
Project is at 91% completion (22/24 phases done).

code.finding: Vault settings UI decisions: new 4th 'Vault' tab on Settings page, 0 disables retention/versioning features, number inputs with preset buttons (7/14/30/90 days), global hard-delete toggle with per-delete confirmation.
Phase 38 scope: migrate callers away from deprecated web services, delete the services, and fix a circular dependency.

workflow: Background agents can be spawned concurrently for executor and planner tasks, allowing parallel phase execution and planning.
Plan files being written to disk is sufficient for the executor agent to proceed — the planner's git commit step is not a blocker.
The GSD dashboard tracks D/P/E columns (presumably Design/Plan/Execute) per phase with status indicators.
When a background agent appears stuck, checking for completed file artifacts on disk can confirm whether the blocking step is cosmetic (commit) vs. substantive.

friction: Phase 38 planner agent got stuck on the git commit step after completing all substantive work, causing user confusion about why it was still running.
Agent branch confusion during commit — the planner logged uncertainty about which branch to commit on.
open_items: Phase 38 executor still running — needs to complete migrating callers, deleting deprecated web services, and fixing the circular dependency.
Phase 39 planner still running — needs to produce PLAN.md files for vault settings implementation.
Phase 38 planner's git commit for plan files is unresolved — plan files exist on disk but may not be committed.
Phase 39 implementation not yet started — depends on Phase 38 completing first.
